messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: intercept in the output of an probitregression with lavaan (two equations, only manifest variables)
parts: I think the negative values of the threshold values - 0,948 and 1,643 are interpretable as the intercepts of the equations? Can anyone explain why Lavaan reports not directly the intercept? (the other coefficients of the equations are nearly the same  in Lavaan and with glm-command)

If you set parameterization = "theta", they should have the same absolute value, but opposite signs.  

The latent response scale is unknown by definition, and so must be arbitrarily identified.  

https://www.statmodel.com/download/webnotes/CatMGLong.pdf

https://doi.org/10.1080/10705510701758406

In the GLM framework, the location and scale of the latent response are typically identified by fixing the threshold to zero (to estimate an intercept) and fixing the residual variance to 1 ("conditional" or "theta" parameterization).  In the SEM framework, the default in Mplus and lavaan is to fix the intercept to zero and estimate the threshold, and to fix the total variance to 1 ("marginal" or "delta" parameterization).  This is arbitrary; either way, the threshold is a certain distance above/below the arbitrary mean of the latent distribution, with units arbitrarily determined by which variance you fix.  Alternatively, you could fix 2 thresholds (in polytomous data) and estimate both the mean/intercept and (residual or marginal) variance given the fixed distance between the 2 fixed thresholds (this approach is used by LISREL).

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam

now I want to compute the margins of the independent variables by hand on the base of the ouput of lavaan (see below for an example) for a probit regression. Normally if you want to compute the margins of the independent variables, you need the value of the intercept. Then you compute:  Fz(value of the intercept). If you want to compute the margin of an independent variable 1 you compute on the base of the Fz(value of the intercept): For example for variable 1: Fz(regression coefficient of variable 1) - Fz(value/coefficient of intercept) = margin of variable 1, if variable 1 is dichotomous. My problem is, that the output of lavaan shows no value of intercept. See below the output, refer as an example to the equation with the dependent 0/1-Variable "Unsicherheit": the coefficient for the independent dichotomous variable "essround_re" is 0.142. But where is the value of the intercept? The intercept of "Unsicherheit" is 0.0000 according to the output (see below). But I think that means, that lavaan didn't compute a intercept !(?). lavaan shows always 0.000 for the intercept in a probitregression.

You can use the GLM formulas you are familiar with if you free the intercept and fix the threshold.  

va01_dummy ~ NA*1 # free intercept
va01_dummy | 0*t1 # fix threshold
